html:
SMTO-AUT-0017 — This sign-in uses an option SMTO doesn't support

GUID: daf6bf7b-7e9f-54c8-97ba-959e91577478
Slug: auth-feature-unsupported
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: auth-broker

What happened

  • The saved sign-in, or the way this task tries to use it, relies on an option SMTO doesn't allow, so SMTO stopped before getting access. It won't turn on an unsupported option just because the service offers it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Send the error details to the person who set up this sign-in in Parameter Store, and ask them to switch it to a sign-in option SMTO supports. The saved sign-in settings decide which option is used, so they are what needs to change.
  2. If the sign-in was made from the Authentication — OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization template and the service has no device sign-in, recreate it from Authentication — Authorized Connection instead. SMTO stops when the service doesn't offer device sign-in, because it can't safely work around that missing step.
  3. After the change, check whether anything the task was meant to send or change already happened. Run it again only if it didn't. The task stopped at the sign-in step, and checking first prevents doing the same action twice.

What success looks like

  • The task gets past the sign-in step without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste secrets into the conversation, and don't keep re-running the task hoping it will pass; the option has to change first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The requested OAuth grant, client authentication method, PAR mode or credential consumer is outside the auth broker's supported set, so authorization was refused.

What this means

  • The requested OAuth grant, authentication extension or consumer/credential binding is outside the supported registered contract. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • The requested OAuth grant, authentication extension or consumer/credential binding is outside the supported registered contract.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact grant, client method and consumer operation with supported broker capabilities.

How to fix it

  • Check the oauth2_client and oauth2_connection profiles in Parameter Store: client_auth_method must be none, client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, client_secret_jwt, private_key_jwt or tls_client_auth; a device_authorization grant needs a provider device_authorization_endpoint; par_mode required needs a pushed_authorization_request_endpoint. The consumer must be registered in CONSUMERS in auth/leases.py (auth, http, gmail, email operations) with credential_type oauth2_bearer and an operation_id.
  • Use a supported grant, client authentication method and registered consumer. Unsupported extensions are not silently enabled.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported method and registered consumer complete the intended authorization without enabling an unreviewed extension.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
